title: Finding a Command You Do Not Know

content.purpose: Find the right command when you know what you want to do but not what it is called.
content.mentalModel: man answers "what does this command do". apropos answers the harder question, "which command does this", by searching every manual page's one-line description for a keyword. whatis is the narrow version: it prints just that one-line description for a page you can already name. Between them you can work out most of Linux without leaving the terminal, which is the point of this module.

demonstration.explanation: One line, straight to the point.
demonstration.output: grep (1) - print lines that match patterns

demonstration.explanation: Every manual page whose description mentions directories. The list is long, which is why you usually pipe it into grep to narrow it down.

remember: apropos searches descriptions by keyword; whatis prints one description
man -k is the same thing as apropos
If apropos finds nothing at all, the manual index may need rebuilding with mandb

tasks.instruction: Get the one-line description of grep and save it to /home/student/whatis-grep.txt.

validators.message: whatis-grep.txt does not mention grep. Check the command you redirected.

hints: One command prints exactly one line about a manual page.
Redirect its output into the file with >.

tasks.context: You need to compare two files line by line but you cannot remember what the command is called.
tasks.instruction: Search the manual descriptions for the keyword compare, and save the results to /home/student/compare-search.txt. The file must mention a command that compares files.

validators.message: compare-search.txt does not include a file comparison command. Search the descriptions for the word compare.

hints: You do not know the command's name, so man will not help. Something searches descriptions instead.
That command is apropos. Give it the keyword compare.
Redirect the search results into the file with >.

reviewQuestions.question: You want to archive some files but cannot remember the command's name. Which tool helps?
reviewQuestions.explanation: apropos searches all page descriptions for a keyword. man and whatis both need the page's actual name.
